mainTopic: Things that come out of non-kosher animals (urine, honey, secretions), and a fish swallowed by another fish
overview: The amud opens as רב ששת finishes explaining why the urine of a non-kosher animal is forbidden. In a second version, the question was only about a חמור's urine, and רב ששת answers from the משנה's rule 'היוצא מן הטמא טמא.' The גמרא challenges him from bee honey, which is permitted even though bees are טמא. It answers that רב ששת follows רבי יעקב, who learns from a פסוק that bee honey is a special Torah exception. That exception does not cover the honey of גזין and wasps. The גמרא then shows that honey which people do not normally eat counts as food only if someone intends to eat it. Next come rulings on other things that come out of animals: lumps discharged by a fallow deer, and the membrane over a newborn donkey's face. רב חסדא and רב הונא debate a ברייתא about the membrane over a human newborn's face. A new משנה then rules that a fish swallowed by another fish keeps its own status. The גמרא asks how we know the inner fish was swallowed and not born, and ends with a ברייתא about which creatures nurse their young.

steps.title: Urine of a non-kosher animal is a non-kosher type
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת finishes his answer. The word 'הטמא' in the פסוק includes anything of a טמא type, and these fluids are of a טמא type.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...the non-kosher.' And these fluids are also a type of non-kosher substance.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud opens at the end of רב ששת's answer to the question about the urine of non-kosher animals. He says the urine is forbidden because it counts as a 'type' of טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'מן הטמא', and רב ששת reads 'מן' as 'מין', meaning any type of non-kosher thing. The urine comes from a טמא animal, so it falls into that category. Therefore it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Non-kosher (here, a non-kosher animal or substance)

phrases.english: '...the non-kosher.'
phrases.notes: This is the last word of a פסוק quoted on the previous amud, so we're jumping in mid-sentence.

phrases.english: And these (fluids) are also a type of non-kosher substance.
phrases.notes: The גמרא reads 'מן הטמא' as 'מין הטמא', meaning any type of טמא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב ששת's answer to his students' question, which began on the previous amud.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Urine of a non-kosher animal is forbidden because it is a 'type' of טמא, derived from the פסוק's word 'הטמא'.

steps.title: Second version: the question was only about donkey urine
steps.stepSummary: A second version (איכא דאמרי) says the students did not ask about horses and camels, since nobody drinks their urine. They asked only about a חמור's urine, which people drink to cure jaundice.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: About horses and camels they had no question, because people do not drink their urine. Their question was about a donkey's urine, which people do drink and which helps cure jaundice. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives a different version of what the students actually asked. This version narrows the question to the urine of a חמור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Horse and camel urine is not an issue, because no one drinks it anyway. Donkey urine is a real practical question, because people drink it as medicine for jaundice. So the students wanted to know whether it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: introduces a second version of the discussion

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question added to the first one. It is a different report of the same conversation, with a narrower question and a different proof.

phrases.english: And there are those who say (a different version):

phrases.aramaic: דְּסוּסִים וּגְמַלִּים לָא קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ,
phrases.english: that about horses and camels they did not have a question,
because people do not drink it.
When they had a question, it was about that of a donkey,
which people drink, and which is good for jaundice.
What is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version of the question that step 1 answered.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a donkey's urine, which people drink as medicine for jaundice, permitted or forbidden?

steps.title: רב ששת answers from the משנה's rule
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers from the משנה: 'What comes from a טמא is טמא.' Donkey urine comes from a טמא animal, so it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to them: You learned it already: What comes out of a non-kosher animal is non-kosher, and what comes out of a kosher animal is kosher. These fluids also come from a non-kosher animal.
steps.whatsHappening: In this second version, רב ששת answers from the general rule of the משנה rather than from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה states a broad principle: anything that comes out of a טמא animal is itself טמא. Donkey urine comes out of a donkey, which is טמא. So it is forbidden, even though people use it as medicine.

keyTerms.meaning: You already learned it (in a משנה)
What comes out of a non-kosher animal is non-kosher

steps.whyThisMatters: 'היוצא מן הטמא טמא' is the central rule of this סוגיא. The coming challenge from bee honey tests just how far this rule reaches.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to them: You learned it:
That which comes out of the non-kosher is non-kosher,
and that which comes out of the kosher is kosher.
And these (fluids) also come from a non-kosher animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the narrowed question raised in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Donkey urine is forbidden, based on the משנה's rule 'היוצא מן הטמא טמא'.

steps.title: Challenge from bee honey
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת from a ברייתא. Bee honey is permitted because bees only carry the nectar inside their bodies; they do not produce it from their bodies.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: Why did they say bee honey is permitted? Because the bees bring it into their bodies, but they do not produce it from their bodies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack רב ששת's ruling. This line sets up a comparison between bee honey and donkey urine, which the גמרא will develop next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bees are טמא, yet their honey is permitted. The ברייתא's reason is that the honey is not made by the bee's body; the bee only carries in nectar from flowers. Urine might be the same: water that enters the body and simply passes out. If so, it should not count as 'coming from a טמא' and should be permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged: the challenge comes from a source of the תנאים (here, a ברייתא)
They bring it into their bodies
They produce (extract) it from their bodies

steps.confusionAlert: Bee honey is not being called kosher-animal produce. Bees are still טמא. The honey is an exception because the bee's body does not produce it.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
For what reason did they say
that bee honey is permitted?
Because they bring it into their bodies,
but they do not produce it from their bodies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב ששת's ruling in step 3 that donkey urine is forbidden.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's ruling that donkey urine is forbidden as 'היוצא מן הטמא'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bee honey is permitted because it only passes through the bee's body and is not produced by it. Urine likewise only passes through the body, so by the same reasoning it should be permitted.

steps.title: רב ששת follows רבי יעקב: the Torah specially permits honey
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת's rule fits the view of רבי יעקב, who holds that honey is permitted only by a special Torah decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said his answer according to רבי יעקב, who says the Torah specifically permitted honey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the ברייתא about bee honey. רב ששת agrees with a different תנא, רבי יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in step 4 said honey is permitted because bees only carry it and do not make it from their bodies. רבי יעקב says honey really does come from the bee. It is permitted only because the Torah made a special exception. So the general rule of רב ששת, 'what comes from a טמא is טמא', still stands, and honey is just an exception.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah or ה׳

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two reasons for permitting honey. The ברייתא in step 4 says honey was never truly 'from' the bee. רבי יעקב says it is from the bee, and the Torah permits it anyway.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רב ששת's rule. Donkey urine stays forbidden, because only honey has a special Torah exception.

phrases.english: He (Rav Sheshet) spoke in accordance with Rabbi Yaakov,
who says: honey, the Merciful One permitted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from the ברייתא about bee honey.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the view to a different תנא (רבי יעקב) who gives a different reason for permitting honey.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Honey being permitted shows that whatever is carried, rather than produced, is permitted. That seems to weaken רב ששת's broad rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Honey is a special Torah exception. The general rule that what comes from a טמא is טמא stays in place.

steps.title: רבי יעקב's source: 'Yet these you may eat'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes רבי יעקב reading the פסוק 'אך את זה תאכלו מכל שרץ העוף'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: רבי יעקב says, 'Yet these you may eat of all flying swarming creatures.' These you may eat, but you may not eat a non-kosher flying swarming creature.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that shows רבי יעקב's view. It begins with his first reading of the פסוק and sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'זה' ('these') seems to limit the permission to the kosher types named in the פסוק. That would mean the non-kosher flying creatures are forbidden. This reading is about to be questioned.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא
flying swarming creatures, such as insects and bees
'yet' or 'only', a limiting word in the פסוק

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yaakov says:
"Yet these you may eat
of all flying swarming creatures" (Vayikra 11:21) —
this you eat,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה אוֹכֵל שֶׁרֶץ עוֹף טָמֵא.
phrases.english: but you do not eat a non-kosher flying swarming creature.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for רבי יעקב's view cited in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יעקב holds honey is permitted by a special Torah decree.

steps.title: That prohibition is already written explicitly
steps.stepSummary: The prohibition of non-kosher flying creatures is already stated clearly in the Torah, so why learn it from 'זה'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But a non-kosher flying swarming creature is already written explicitly as forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The text objects to the reading just given. Why do we need the word 'זה' to teach something the Torah already says openly?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous פסוק (ויקרא 11:20) already forbids non-kosher flying swarming creatures. So the reading in step 6 would make the extra words pointless. They must be teaching something new.

phrases.english: A non-kosher flying swarming creature is written explicitly!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the simple reading of the פסוק in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'זה' comes to forbid non-kosher flying creatures.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק should not be read to teach something already stated explicitly elsewhere. That would make the words extra.

steps.title: The verse permits what a non-kosher flying creature emits: bee honey
steps.stepSummary: The real lesson is that you may eat what a non-kosher flying creature produces, namely bee honey.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it this way: a non-kosher flying swarming creature itself you may not eat, but you may eat what a non-kosher flying creature emits. What is that? Bee honey.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a new reading of the פסוק. The extra word is teaching that bee honey is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The creature itself stays forbidden. What it emits (משריץ) is permitted by this פסוק. That is a special Torah permission for honey, exactly as רבי יעקב was quoted in step 5.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁרֶץ עוֹף טָמֵא אִי אַתָּה אוֹכֵל,
phrases.english: Rather: a non-kosher flying swarming creature you do not eat,
but you do eat
what a non-kosher flying creature emits,
and which is this? This is bee honey.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שֶׁרֶץ עוֹף טָמֵא אִי אַתָּה אוֹכֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the objection in step 7 by rereading the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the פסוק so the extra word teaches a new law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'זה' only repeats the ban on non-kosher flying creatures.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'זה' permits what a non-kosher flying creature emits, which is bee honey.

steps.title: Honey of גזין and wasps is not included
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that the permission does not extend to the honey of גזין and wasps.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that even the honey of גזין and wasps is permitted. You must say: no.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא limits the new permission. Only bee honey is included, not honey from other insects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once honey from a non-kosher creature is allowed, one might extend this to all insect honey. The ברייתא rules this out. The reason is not given yet, and it sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: a type of honey-making insect, perhaps a kind of hornet

phrases.english: One might think: even the honey of gazin and wasps?
You said: no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the permission derived in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only bee honey is permitted, not the honey of גזין or wasps.

steps.title: Why include bees and exclude גזין and wasps?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what reason there is to include bee honey but exclude other insect honey.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see to include bees and to exclude גזין and wasps?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks for the reason behind the limit it just set. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All of these insects are non-kosher flying creatures that make honey. So the difference needs a basis.

keyTerms.meaning: what did you see, meaning what is your reason

phrases.english: And what did you see to include bees,
and to exclude gazin and wasps?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the limit set in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What distinguishes bee honey from the honey of other insects.

steps.title: Bee honey has no qualifying name; the others do
steps.stepSummary: Bee honey is simply called 'honey', while the other kinds always need a qualifying word.
steps.simpleTranslation: I include bee honey, because it has no added name. I exclude the honey of גזין and wasps, because it has an added name.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers. Plain 'honey' means bee honey, so only bee honey counts as the honey the Torah permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When people say just 'honey', they mean bee honey. Other honeys must be named with a qualifier, such as 'wasp honey'. So only bee honey falls within the permission.
steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת holds like רבי יעקב. What comes from a טמא is טמא, and bee honey is a special Torah exception learned from 'אך את זה'. The exception covers only plain 'honey', meaning bee honey. So donkey urine stays forbidden.

phrases.english: I include bee honey
which has no qualifying name,
and I exclude the honey of gazin and wasps
which has a qualifying name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bee honey is called plain 'honey'. Other honeys need a qualifying name, so they are excluded.

steps.title: Whose view permits the honey of גזין and wasps?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא is behind a ברייתא that calls the honey of גזין and wasps טהור and permitted to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion matches the ברייתא that says: the honey of גזין and wasps is pure and permitted to eat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא and asks which opinion it follows. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, the ברייתא of רבי יעקב said that only bee honey is permitted and that the honey of גזין and wasps is excluded. This new ברייתא says the opposite, so the גמרא wants to know who holds it.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of bee-like insect (exact species unclear)
Here: not susceptible to food impurity unless someone intends to eat it (step 14 explains)

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is that which was taught in a baraita:
The honey of gizzin and wasps
is pure and permitted to eat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares a new ברייתא with רבי יעקב's ruling that excluded the honey of גזין and wasps.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that the honey of גזין and wasps is permitted?

steps.title: It is not like רבי יעקב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that permits the honey of גזין and wasps does not follow רבי יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not in accordance with רבי יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this ברייתא disagrees with רבי יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יעקב permitted only bee honey, because only bee honey is called plain 'honey'. This ברייתא permits the honey of other insects too, so it must follow a different תנא, who does not limit the permission to bees.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who permitted only bee honey

phrases.english: It is not in accordance with Rabbi Ya'akov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows a תנא who disagrees with רבי יעקב and permits the honey of גזין and wasps.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views: רבי יעקב permits only bee honey, while another ברייתא permits the honey of גזין and wasps too.

steps.title: 'Pure' shows this honey needs intent to count as food
steps.stepSummary: The word 'טהור' teaches that the honey of גזין and wasps can only become impure as food if someone intends to eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Pure': this shows that it requires intention to eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a lesson from the word 'טהור' in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something only becomes impure as food if it counts as food. People do not usually eat the honey of גזין and wasps, so it is not food until someone decides to eat it. This means that by default it stays טהור. By implication, bee honey is normal food and needs no special intent.

keyTerms.meaning: Intention (here, to use it as food)

steps.confusionAlert: 'טהור' here does not mean the honey can never become impure. It means it cannot become impure until a person intends to eat it.

phrases.english: 'Pure' — evidently it requires intention.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes a word inside the ברייתא quoted in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The honey of גזין and wasps is susceptible to טומאת אוכלין only if someone intends to eat it.

steps.title: A ברייתא: bee honey is food even without intent
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports this: bee honey still in its hive can become impure as food without any special intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: honey in its hive becomes impure with food impurity even without intention.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the idea just stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bee honey is normal food, so it counts as food automatically, even while it is still in the hive. This confirms the contrast: other insect honey needs intent, while bee honey does not.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a supporting ברייתא)
The impurity that applies to food

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
Honey in its hive becomes impure
with food impurity, without intention.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the inference of step 14.
steps.raayaObject: Bee honey is food on its own, but other insect honey needs intent.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: 'דבש בכוורתו מטמא טומאת אוכלין שלא במחשבה'.
steps.whatToRemember: Bee honey counts as food automatically. The honey of גזין and wasps counts as food only if someone intends to eat it.

steps.title: The Sages assumed the lumps from a fallow deer were forbidden eggs
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן first thought that the lumps that come out of a יחמורתא are egg cells and are therefore forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Concerning the lumps of the fallow deer, the Sages thought to say: they are eggs, and they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic about another secretion and states the Sages' first assumption. This sets up רב ספרא's correction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lumps were the animal's own egg cells, they would be part of a living animal and forbidden as אבר מן החי. The phrase 'סבור רבנן למימר' signals that this is only an initial assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: Lumps or passages that are discharged
The Sages thought to say (an assumption that is later corrected)

phrases.english: The lumps of the fallow deer —
the Sages thought to say:
they are eggs, and they are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case about secretions that come from animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Initial assumption: the lumps are egg cells and are forbidden.

steps.title: רב ספרא: the lumps are a hart's semen
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא explains that the lumps are hardened semen from an איל that mated with the יחמורתא, not her own egg cells.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said: It is the seed of a hart. The hart goes after the hind, but since her womb is narrow she does not mate with it. So it goes after the fallow deer, and the lumps fall out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא rejects the Sages' assumption by explaining where the lumps really come from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lumps are not part of the female animal's body. They are semen from a different animal that hardened and fell out. Because of this, the reason for forbidding them (that they are part of a living animal) no longer applies.

phrases.english: Rav Safra said:
It is the semen of a hart,
which goes after the hind,
and since her womb is narrow, she does not mate with it,
so it goes after the fallow deer, and the lumps fall out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא זַרְעָא דְּאַיָּלָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the assumption of step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the Sages' assumption that the lumps are egg cells and therefore forbidden.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The Sages misidentified the lumps. They are hardened semen from an איל, not part of the female animal.
steps.whatToRemember: The lumps from a יחמורתא are hardened semen from an איל, so the reason to forbid them falls away.

steps.title: רב הונא: the membrane over a newborn donkey's face is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that the skin covering a donkey's face at birth is permitted, because it is only a secretion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The skin that comes out over a donkey's face is permitted. What is the reason? It is merely a secretion.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a new ruling about another animal secretion and explains his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though a donkey is a non-kosher animal, this membrane (the fetal sac) is not a real part of the mother or the foal. It is only a secretion, so it is not forbidden as part of a non-kosher animal.
steps.whatToRemember: A secretion that is not truly part of an animal's body is not forbidden, even when it comes from a non-kosher animal.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹר הַבָּא כְּנֶגֶד פָּנָיו שֶׁל חֲמוֹר — מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: The skin that comes out over the face of a donkey is permitted.
What is the reason?
It is merely a secretion.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא עוֹר הַבָּא כְּנֶגֶד פָּנָיו שֶׁל חֲמוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling in the series on secretions from animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The membrane over a newborn donkey's face is permitted, because it is merely a secretion.

steps.title: רב חסדא brings a ברייתא that seems to support רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא quotes a ברייתא: the skin over a newborn person's face is טהור whether alive or dead. He suggests this means even when both baby and mother are dead, so the skin is just a secretion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: There is a ברייתא that supports you. The skin that comes over the face of a person at birth, whether alive or dead, is טהור. Doesn't that mean: whether the baby and mother are both alive, or the baby and mother are both dead?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא is offering proof for רב הונא's ruling from the previous step. The proof is a ברייתא about the skin over a human baby's face.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this skin were a real body part, it would carry טומאת מת when baby and mother are both dead. The ברייתא says it is טהור even when they are dead. That would show the skin is only a secretion, just as רב הונא said about the donkey. The proof only works if 'dead' means both of them are dead.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא is taught that supports you
The skin (membrane) that comes over the face at birth
Ritually pure; here, it does not carry corpse impurity
Is it not that…? (introduces a proposed reading)

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to him (to Rav Huna):
It is taught in a baraita in a way that supports you:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹר הַבָּא כְּנֶגֶד פָּנָיו שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: The skin that comes over the face of a person (a newborn),
whether alive or dead — is pure.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו בֵּין הוּא חַי וְאִמּוֹ חַיָּה,
phrases.english: Does it not mean: whether he is alive and his mother is alive,
or he is dead and his mother is dead?
phrases.notes: If both are dead and the skin is still pure, it must be only a secretion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רב הונא's ruling in step 18
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's claim that the skin over a newborn donkey's face is only a secretion (פירשא בעלמא), shown from the parallel case of a human newborn
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא saying the skin over a human newborn's face is טהור 'whether alive or dead'

steps.title: The ברייתא may mean that only one of them is alive
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rejects the proof. 'Alive or dead' may mean that one of the two is alive: the baby alive and the mother dead, or the baby dead and the mother alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It may mean: whether he is alive and his mother is dead, or he is dead and his mother is alive.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא rejects the proof by reading the ברייתא differently. In his reading, the skin is טהור only when at least one of them is alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not explain why the skin would be טהור when one of them is alive. The point is only that the ברייתא could be speaking about cases where someone is alive. In that case the ברייתא says nothing about when both are dead. So it no longer proves the skin is only a secretion.

phrases.english: No,
it means whether he is alive and his mother is dead,
or he is dead and his mother is alive.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, בֵּין הוּא חַי וְאִמּוֹ מֵתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of the ברייתא offered in step 19
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this proof, not the ruling itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Alive or dead' could mean that only one of them is alive, so the ברייתא tells us nothing about when both are dead

steps.title: A second ברייתא says explicitly that both are alive or both are dead
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers with another ברייתא that clearly says 'both alive or both dead.' This removes the alternate reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: whether he is alive and his mother is alive, or he is dead and his mother is dead?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא brings a ברייתא with explicit wording that blocks רב הונא's alternate reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא spells out the exact case רב חסדא wanted, including 'both dead.' So the skin is טהור even with no living person involved. That shows it is only a secretion.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא…! (brings a source to counter a claim)

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:
whether he is alive and his mother is alive,
or he is dead and his mother is dead!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters the rejection in step 20 with an explicit source
steps.raayaObject: That the skin is only a secretion and stays טהור even when both are dead
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that explicitly says 'he is dead and his mother is dead'

steps.title: If that ברייתא exists, it is accepted
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא concedes: if that ברייתא is taught, then it is taught, and the proof stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is taught, it is taught.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא accepts the explicit ברייתא and stops arguing. The proof for his own ruling now stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra reading in step 20 was only a possible way to push off the first proof. Once an explicit source settles it, there is nothing left to argue. The conclusion is that the facial skin is only a secretion, which fits רב הונא's ruling that it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is taught, it is taught (I accept the source)

steps.whatToRemember: The skin over a newborn's face is treated as a mere secretion. It is טהור even when baby and mother are both dead, and it is permitted on an animal, as רב הונא ruled.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't get confused that רב הונא pushes off a proof that supports his own ruling. In step 20 he is only showing that the first ברייתא was not airtight proof. Once the explicit ברייתא is quoted, he accepts it.

phrases.english: If it is taught, it is taught.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the source brought in step 21
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The explicit ברייתא is accepted. The facial skin is only a secretion, which supports רב הונא.

steps.title: משנה: a fish swallowed by another fish keeps its own status
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a kosher fish found inside a non-kosher fish is permitted. A non-kosher fish found inside a kosher fish is forbidden, because it did not grow from the fish that swallowed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A non-kosher fish that swallowed a kosher fish: the kosher fish may be eaten. A kosher fish that swallowed a non-kosher fish: the non-kosher fish may not be eaten. This is because it is not the product of the fish it was found in.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: a fish found inside another fish. It rules that the inner fish keeps its own status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, what comes from a non-kosher animal is forbidden, and what comes from a kosher animal is permitted. Here the inner fish was only swallowed, not born from the outer fish. So the outer fish's status does not pass to it. That is the meaning of 'לפי שאינו גידולו.'

keyTerms.meaning: Its product; what grew from it

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the general rule: what comes from a forbidden creature is forbidden only when it actually grew from that creature.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A non-kosher fish that swallowed a kosher fish:
the kosher fish is permitted to be eaten,
and a kosher fish that swallowed a non-kosher fish:
the non-kosher fish is forbidden to be eaten,
because it is not its product (it did not grow from the outer fish).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ דָּג טָמֵא שֶׁבָּלַע דָּג טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It ties loosely to the theme of what counts as the product of an animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A swallowed fish keeps its own kosher status, since it is not the product of the fish that swallowed it.

steps.title: The משנה applies only when we saw the fish being swallowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה: the kosher fish is permitted only because we saw it being swallowed. If we did not see this, we assume the non-kosher fish gave birth to it, so it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that we saw it swallow. But if we did not see it swallow, we say that it spawned it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads a hidden condition into the משנה. A kosher fish found inside a non-kosher fish is permitted only if we saw it being swallowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Swallowed' in the משנה means the swallowing was actually seen. Without seeing it, the more natural assumption is that the inner fish is the offspring of the outer non-kosher fish. As its product, it would be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is only because… (introduces an inference)
It spawned it (gave birth to it)

steps.confusionAlert: This inference is about the first case only: a kosher fish found inside a non-kosher one. If we did not see the swallowing, the kosher-looking fish is forbidden, because we assume it is the non-kosher fish's offspring.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The reason (it is permitted) is that we saw it swallow,
but if we did not see it swallow —
we say: it spawned it.
phrases.notes: So the inner fish would count as the non-kosher fish's product and be forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a limiting inference from the wording of the משנה in step 23
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The kosher fish inside a non-kosher fish is permitted only if the swallowing was seen. Otherwise we assume it was born from the outer fish, so it is forbidden.

steps.title: What is the source for this worry?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know to worry that a non-kosher fish gave birth to the kosher fish found inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for the idea in step 24. This one word sets up the next step, where the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 said that if we did not see the swallowing, we assume the non-kosher fish gave birth to the fish inside it. That is a surprising idea, because the fish inside looks kosher. So the גמרא wants a source showing that non-kosher fish give birth in a way that could explain this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
phrases.notes: Asks for the source of the worry stated in step 24.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the inference made in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What source tells us that a non-kosher fish may have given birth to the fish found inside it?

steps.title: Non-kosher fish give birth, kosher fish lay eggs
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a non-kosher fish gives birth to live young, while a kosher fish lays eggs.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: A non-kosher fish gives birth to live young. A kosher fish lays eggs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a ברייתא. Non-kosher fish give birth to live young, so a live fish found inside one could be its own baby.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A kosher fish lays eggs, so its young hatch outside its body. A non-kosher fish carries live young inside it. So a small fish found inside a non-kosher fish might be its baby, and the baby of a non-kosher fish is non-kosher, even if it looks kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the fish inside must be kosher just because it looks kosher. The point is that the baby of a non-kosher fish is non-kosher, whatever it looks like.

phrases.english: As it is taught: a non-kosher fish gives birth to live young,
a kosher fish lays eggs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא teaches that non-kosher fish give birth to live young, so a fish found inside a non-kosher fish could be its own baby.

steps.title: Even if we saw the swallowing, maybe this is a newborn
steps.stepSummary: If non-kosher fish give birth to live young, then even when we saw the swallowing, maybe the swallowed fish was digested and this fish is a newborn.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even when we see that it swallowed a fish, we should say: that swallowed fish was digested, and this fish is one the non-kosher fish gave birth to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the case where the משנה permits the fish. If non-kosher fish give birth, why trust that the fish we found is the one we saw being swallowed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 said seeing the swallowing makes the fish permitted. But seeing a swallow does not prove that this fish is the swallowed one. The swallowed fish could have been digested, and the fish we found could be a newborn. Then the fish should be forbidden even in the משנה's case.

phrases.english: If so, when we see that it swallowed,
we should say: that one was digested,
phrases.notes: The fish that was swallowed is gone.

phrases.english: and this one, it gave birth to it!
phrases.notes: The fish we found is its newborn, so it should be forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא of step 26 to attack the permitted case of the משנה as read in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the משנה (step 24) that seeing the swallowing makes the fish permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If non-kosher fish give birth to live young, seeing a swallow does not prove that the fish found is the swallowed one. It may have been digested and replaced by a newborn.

steps.title: רב ששת: It was found in the digestive tract
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the משנה is speaking about a fish found in the path of waste, not where babies grow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: The case is where it was found in the path of the waste.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the challenge. The fish was found in the digestive tract, where swallowed food goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baby fish would grow in the womb area, not in the digestive tract. If the kosher fish is found where food passes, it clearly was swallowed and not born. So there is no fear that it is a newborn.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, the case is where
The path of the waste (the digestive tract)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
Such as where he found it in the path of the waste.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any fish found inside could be a newborn, even after we saw a swallow.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the fish is found in the digestive tract, it was clearly swallowed, so it is permitted.

steps.title: רב פפא: It was found in the gullet
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the משנה is speaking about a fish found in the throat passage of the swallowing fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The case is where it was found in the passage of the throat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives another answer to the same challenge. The fish was found in the gullet, the path a swallowed fish goes down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same type of answer as רב ששת, but with a different location. A fish in the throat passage was clearly just swallowed and was not born there.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Such as where he found it in the path of the gullet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel answer to the challenge of step 27, alongside רב ששת.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The found fish could be a newborn.
steps.terutzMaskana: A fish found in the gullet was clearly swallowed, so it is permitted.

steps.title: רב נחמן: It was found whole and full-sized
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the משנה is speaking about a fish found whole and fully grown, not like a newborn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The case is where it was found whole.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a third answer. He looks at how the fish looks, not at where it was found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A newborn fish is tiny and not fully formed. If the fish inside is whole and full-sized, it cannot be a newborn, so it must be the one that was swallowed.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Such as where he found it whole.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר כְּגוֹן שֶׁמְּצָאוֹ שָׁלֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third parallel answer to step 27, based on the fish's condition instead of its location.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The found fish could be a newborn.
steps.terutzMaskana: A whole, full-grown fish cannot be a newborn, so it is permitted.

steps.title: רב אשי: Most fish give birth to their own kind
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says we do not need to see the swallowing. Most fish give birth to their own species, so a kosher fish inside a non-kosher fish was surely swallowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Most fish give birth to their own kind, so it is as if it swallowed it in front of us.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי takes a whole different approach. He rejects the idea that the משנה needs us to see the swallowing at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most fish give birth only to fish of their own species. So a kosher-type fish inside a non-kosher fish is almost surely not its baby. Following the רוב, we treat it as if we saw it swallowed, and it is permitted. This removes both the inference of step 24 and the challenge of step 27.

keyTerms.meaning: The majority (we follow what usually happens)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain the משנה. רב ששת, רב פפא, and רב נחמן say we saw the swallowing and point to a clear sign that the fish was not born there. רב אשי says no sign is needed, because most fish give birth to their own kind.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב אשי's approach changes the practical result. A kosher fish found inside a non-kosher fish is permitted even if no one saw it being swallowed.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Most fish give birth to their own kind,
and it is considered as if it swallowed in front of us.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר רוֹב דָּגִים בְּמִינָן מַשְׁרִיצִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Instead of narrowing the case like steps 28-30, it rejects the starting assumption of step 24 that the swallowing must be seen.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the premise and using רוב (majority)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה permits the fish only when we saw it being swallowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because most fish give birth to their own kind, a kosher fish inside a non-kosher fish is treated as swallowed, even if no one saw it.

steps.title: The full ברייתא: who nurses and who gathers food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the full ברייתא. Creatures that give birth nurse their young, creatures that lay eggs gather food for them, and the bat lays eggs yet nurses.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A non-kosher fish gives birth to live young. A kosher fish lays eggs. Every creature that gives birth nurses its young. Every creature that lays eggs gathers food for its young. The exception is the bat: even though it lays eggs, it nurses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the whole ברייתא that it used in step 26. This adds a new general rule about how animals feed their young.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half repeats the fish rule from step 26. The new part is a general rule: animals that give birth nurse, and animals that lay eggs gather food. The bat is an exception: it lays eggs, as the ברייתא states, but still nurses.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: A non-kosher fish gives birth to live young,
a kosher fish lays eggs,
every creature that gives birth nurses,
and every creature that lays eggs gathers food for its young,
except for the bat,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמֵּטִיל בֵּיצִים — מֵנִיק.
phrases.english: which, even though it lays eggs, nurses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes in full the ברייתא that step 26 cited only in part.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Creatures that give birth nurse their young, and creatures that lay eggs gather food for them, except for the bat, which lays eggs and still nurses.
